ai.description: *Micrixalus nudis* is a small frog (20–25 mm) with a brown, granular dorsum and pale throat. It is distinguished by a distinct white snout tip and the male's characteristic foot-flagging behavior.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Micrixalus nudis* is best distinguished by the absence of a distinct white or pale-colored glandular fold on the dorsum, which is present in most other dancing frog species.
ai.habitat: *Micrixalus nudis* inhabits the rocky, fast-flowing streams of evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found at mid-to-high elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Naked Dancing Frog is primarily diurnal, with males performing a unique "foot-flagging" display by extending and waving their hind legs to attract mates near streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Micrixalus nudis* is an egg-laying species that deposits small clutches of eggs in stream-bed crevices. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically June–August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Micrixalus nudis* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically inhabiting streams in the states of Karnataka and Kerala at elevations between 400 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The *Micrixalus nudis* call is a high-pitched, rhythmic series of short, metallic chirps emitted by males while foot-flagging near fast-flowing forest streams.
